_comment: Ontology-projection declaration completeness over the LIVE microservice-manifest corpus. Until governance/check/ontology-projection-coverage/tests/ontology_projection_coverage_live.rs landed, this doctrine had never produced a verdict about this codebase: the crate's only Cargo consumer was marketplace/facade/dev-cli, which no workflow invokes, so every case it had ever run was a hand-written fixture inside src/lib.rs. Three sets are pinned here and every one is pinned by EQUALITY over the UNION of the frozen and observed keys, so all three are TWO-SIDED: a new observation blocks, and a frozen observation that stops being produced ALSO blocks until it is struck in the same change. The min_* floors count SUBJECT files, manifests, and projection entries -- never findings -- so no floor here can red on honest progress.
authority: ADR-0701 (live apex; carries the ADR-0145 residual) + specs/microservices/manifest-schema.json
_authority_note: The originating clause is ADR-0145 Invariant 3, which is Superseded by ADR-0701. ADR-0701's `ADR-145 residual` section restates Invariant 1 only and is truncated before Invariant 3, so the LIVE requirement that every manifest carry an `ontology_projections` block does NOT rest on restated apex prose -- it rests on specs/microservices/manifest-schema.json, which lists `ontology_projections` in its top-level `required` array and names this crate as its validator. That spec is the authority this gate enforces; the ADR ids are provenance. Stated here rather than left implicit, because a doctrine resting only on a retired ADR would be a delete candidate rather than a connect one.
subject: every tracked file whose basename is exactly `manifest.json`; the owning microservice is the manifest's own DECLARED `"microservice"` value, never its directory leaf
_leaf_keying_is_wrong_and_this_is_the_me: CANONICAL_ENTITY_OWNERS is a list of BARE microservice names, so how a caller derives the name from a manifest decides which manifests are subjects at all. Keying on the directory leaf is wrong in BOTH directions on this tree, measured, not assumed: `audit/manifest.json` declares "audit-chain", which IS an owner, so a leaf-keyed run drops a real subject; `network/manifest.json` declares "cloud-network", which is NOT an owner, so a leaf-keyed run invents a subject the doctrine never named. `frozen_owner_manifests` freezes the resolved binding itself, so a manifest that renames its declared microservice out of the owner set cannot silently shrink the subject.
_measured_2026_08_19: Measured on dev @ 889027711 (the commit that deleted 51 unreferenced product crates): 13746 tracked paths, 89 manifest.json files, 47 containing an `ontology_projections` key, 20 declaring a NON-EMPTY projection list, 74 projection entries, 13 manifests owned by a canonical-entity owner. Strict-mode findings: ZERO. That zero is evidence rather than vacuity because the subject is large and named: the floors below pin 80 manifests, 11 owner manifests, and 60 projection entries, so the walk cannot collapse to nothing and report a disciplined tree.
_foundry_is_matchable_contrary_to_expect: `foundry` in CANONICAL_ENTITY_OWNERS was suspected unmatchable because no top-level `foundry/` directory exists. It matches anyway: oya/intelligence/_legacy-foundry/manifest.json declares "microservice": "foundry". The genuinely unmatchable owner is `network` -- see frozen_unmatched_owners.
_frozen_strict_findings_note: Keyed `<manifest path>::<kernel summary>`. Empty TODAY, and empty is the correct pin: every one of the 13 owner manifests declares at least one concrete projection with a non-empty entity_name and projection_target_table, and no manifest fails to parse. Pinned by equality, so a manifest that starts violating the doctrine blocks immediately (born-blocking; the debt cannot grow silently). This is NOT a floor on a zero-target term -- it is an equality-pinned set, which reds on regression and never on repair.
_frozen_unmatched_owners_note: Canonical-entity owner names that no tracked manifest declares, so the doctrine names them and enforces nothing. `network` is the only one: network/manifest.json declares "cloud-network". Frozen as a set rather than a count so the entry is attributable, and two-sided so neither a new dangling owner name nor a quietly-repaired one passes unrecorded. Repairing this entry means either renaming the declared microservice or dropping `network` from CANONICAL_ENTITY_OWNERS -- both are edits to reviewable text, and both must strike this entry in the same change.
